Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City htto: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 37 s. 2023 MAY It 2023 Mr. ROMMEL LEE B. ANCHETA President Alliance of Basic Education Leaders and Teachers Blk 3 lot 1 Bulacan Meadows Subdv., Cay Pombo, Sta. Maria Bulacan Dear Mr. Ancheta: This has reference to your letter dated October 3, 2022 seeking legal opinion from this Department on the remedies available to get the e-vehicle project continued as intended to be able to serve the public and use the government resources and finances as this was suspended by the new mayor. Per your letter, you entered into a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with the City of Imus, Cavite for the following purposes: (a) providing emergency and assistance in times of calamities, referral and communications network for humanitarian efforts within the City of Imus, Cavite; (b) reducing the impact of pollution; (c) promoting the movement of residents; (d) decrease the adverse social and economic impact of the pandemic; and (e) generate employment. Generally, you agreed to corroborate in fulfilling the abovementioned purposes by providing alternative livelihood project known as E-VEHICLE PROJECT that would deliver an advanced transport system that would cater the riding public of City of Imus. You then stated that the City Ordinance of Imus No. 03-2015 series of 2019 supports this MOA. However, you alleged that said MOA and the implementation of the ordinance was suspended by the new mayor of Imus. Hence, the request for a remedy to get the project be continued. At the outset, we deem it proper to highlight the definition of a Memorandum of Agreement, which is a legal document describing a business partnership between two parties that have agreed to cooperate to meet an agreed objective or complete a project. The memorandum lays out the agreed terms and outlines the steps to reach the desired goal of the agreement. 1 Also, we find the attached MOA entered into by and between City of Imus, Cavite and 1 Memorandum of Agreement, Contracts Counsel, https://www.contractscounsel.com/t/us/memorandum-of-agreement "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Alliance of Basic Education Leaders and Teachers material in addressing the subject query. In this regard, in a MOA, the governing laws are the provisions of the New Civil Code of the Philippines on partnerships and contracts, considering that it is akin to partnerships. Correspondingly, under our civil laws, a contract is the law between the parties. Obligations arising from contracts have the force of law between the contracting parties should be complied with in good faith. In other words, the agreement or contracts between the parties is the formal expression of the parties' rights, duties, and obligations.2 Thus, when the terms of an agreement have been reduced to writing, it is considered as containing all the terms agreed upon and there can be no evidence of such terms other than the contents of the written agreement between the parties and their successors in interest.3 Accordingly, we are of the view that the MOA between City of Imus, Cavite and Alliance of Basic Education Leaders and Teachers is governed by the provisions in their agreement, which includes the termination clause, as well as, clause on dispute resolution and venue regarding enforcement of any right under the agreement. Hence, the change of administration cannot perse detract the parties to comply with the agreements set forth in the contract as this is not a ground for termination of the subject MOA. The parties also cannot unilaterally rescind the contract, any action to do the same should be thru the appropriate courts.4 The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AU OF THE SECRETARY: VICTOR R.
